payload.purpose_context: Seven small defects reported against 4.0.0rc9 each make a status, planning or glossary command fail, refuse valid input, or silently lose information: the status event log reader splits rows on characters that are not line breaks and lets JSON-limit errors escape its documented error type; the log writer can emit non-standard NaN/Infinity numbers and Windows line endings; the event sanitiser crashes on a mixed naive/aware session pair; the two work package task-file locators disagree on letter case; map-shaped subtask entries are silently coerced so the for_review gate can never pass; a mission meta.json with a UTF-8 byte-order mark makes the Mission invisible; and glossary conflict listing slows quadratically. This mission fixes each with the smallest change that converges core on the rulings spec-kitty-events already records, and repairs the one in-repo Mission (058) whose data the stricter subtask rule would otherwise refuse.
payload.purpose_tldr: Fix seven small, independently reported defects in the status event log, work package task-file reading, mission metadata loading and glossary conflict listing.

options: The seven issues #7439 #7440 #7441 #7442 #7443 #7445 #7463 plus the Mission 058 data repair; other splitters/locators/meta readers recorded as follow-ups
payload.question: Which issues does this mission cover, and what is explicitly out of scope?

payload.final_answer: The seven issues #7439 #7440 #7441 #7442 #7443 #7445 #7463 plus the one-off Mission 058 data repair. Out of scope (recorded as follow-up issues): JSONL splitters outside status/store.py (merge driver, lifecycle_events, status_service, bookkeeping_projection, migrate_lifecycle_envelope), the remaining WP-file locators with their own case rules (dependency_graph, task_utils/support, workspace/context), a single BOM policy in the kernel meta decoder, and draining the archive-gate sanctioned-correction entry after merge. No version bump.

options: One shared line splitter (LF, CRLF, lone CR only) plus one decode helper mapping ValueError/RecursionError to StoreError across the store.py readers
payload.question: #7439: how should the status event-log readers frame rows and report JSON-limit failures?

payload.final_answer: One shared line splitter in status/store.py that ends a row only at LF, CRLF or a lone CR, used by every store.py text reader (seed_scratch_event_log, the strict text readers, read_events_lenient); and one decode helper that maps ValueError (incl. the 4300-digit integer limit) and RecursionError (deep nesting) to StoreError for the strict readers, a skipped row for the lenient reader, and ValueError for seed_scratch_event_log (its documented type). Splitters outside store.py are a follow-up issue.

options: Refuse non-finite numbers (allow_nan=False, refusal as StoreError, nothing written) and write LF-only on every OS (newline="\n"); red test asserts the temp file newline
payload.question: #7441: what must the status event-log writer guarantee about numbers and line endings?

payload.final_answer: Refuse non-finite numbers: serialisation uses allow_nan=False and a NaN/Infinity value refuses as StoreError naming the event, with nothing written. Write LF line endings on every OS by opening the temp file with newline set to LF; the red-first test asserts the newline argument of the temp-file open (CPython on Linux cannot observe CRLF), plus a portable byte pin with no CRLF. After the fix the serialised line equals the spec-kitty-events byte rule.

options: Drop both session timestamps and emit no duration, per the sanitiser docs (malformed is removed silently)
payload.question: #7440: what should the event sanitiser do with a naive session_started_at paired with an aware session_ended_at (or the reverse)?

payload.final_answer: Treat the mixed naive/aware pair as unparseable: drop both session timestamps and emit no session_duration_s, with no exception, as the sanitiser docstring already promises for malformed timestamps. Do not invent a timezone. Two naive or two aware timestamps keep computing a duration.

options: One shared locator in core: case-insensitive id, separator tail, README excluded, non-regular-file matches fail closed; dependency, roster and WP view all use it
Make the dependency locator case-insensitive only
payload.question: #7443: how should the work package task-file locators match a WP id?

payload.final_answer: One shared locator in the core layer used by the dependency guard, the subtask roster and the WP view: WP id matched case-insensitively with the existing separator tail, README excluded case-insensitively (the spec-kitty-events R26 rule). A match that is not a regular file (directory, dangling link) makes the gate readers fail closed (roster: SubtaskRosterResolutionError; dependency read: unresolvable TransitionError) and the read-only view/mirror treat it as no file. Other locators (dependency_graph, task_utils/support, workspace/context) are a follow-up.

options: Refuse with SubtaskRosterResolutionError naming the WP file and the expected list form; repair Mission 058 once in the same PR
Read the id key from maps
payload.question: #7442: what happens to a subtasks: entry that is not a task id (a map, list, float, date, boolean or null)?

payload.final_answer: Refuse: the roster accepts only string or integer (not boolean) entries; anything else, and an integer too long to convert (more than 4300 digits), raises SubtaskRosterResolutionError naming the WP file and the expected list form (e.g. '- T001'). The WP view catches it and shows an empty authored subtask list. The spec states that mark-status then refuses for the whole Mission until the file is fixed. Mission 058's 28 map entries in its six WP files are repaired once in the same PR via a dated _OPERATOR_SANCTIONED_CORRECTIONS entry in tests/architectural/test_archive_root_byte_identical.py; removing that entry after merge is a follow-up named in the PR body. Operator decision 2026-11-10.

options: Option A: load_meta and parse_meta_file read with utf-8-sig; kernel decode_meta unchanged
Option B: make the kernel decoder BOM-tolerant
payload.question: #7445: how should mission meta.json loading treat a UTF-8 byte-order mark?

payload.final_answer: Option A (operator decision 2026-11-10): load_meta and parse_meta_file decode meta.json with utf-8-sig, so a BOM-prefixed file reads like the same file without one; strictly widening, non-BOM files decode identically. kernel decode_meta is not changed; load_meta_strict(bom_tolerant=False) stays the negative control. The remaining BOM-rejecting readers (planning_commit, ref_advance, mission_finalize, charter activation) are a documented residual and a follow-up.

options: Hoist the existing-id set out of the loop and add each appended id, preserving de-duplication; deterministic tests only, timings recorded in the PR
payload.question: #7463: how is the quadratic conflict rescan fixed and proven?

payload.final_answer: Build the set of known conflict ids once before the resolved-event pass and add each newly appended id to it, so a repeated resolved event still yields one conflict (dedup preserved). Proof is deterministic: a characterisation test for repeated resolved ids and a scale test asserting 2n conflicts for n requested plus n resolved. No wall-clock performance test; before/after timings are recorded in the PR body.

options: Five WPs: store+sanitizer; locator+roster+view+emit locator+archive-gate entry; meta BOM; glossary; Mission 058 data repair (planning_artifact, depends on the roster WP)
payload.question: How is the work split into work packages with non-overlapping owned files?

payload.final_answer: Five WPs (operator split 2026-11-10): WP01 status/store.py + events/sanitizer.py (#7439 #7441 #7440); WP02 new core/wp_task_files.py + core/subtask_rows.py + the status/emit.py WP-file locator only + status/wp_view.py + the archive-gate sanctioned-correction entry (#7443 #7442); WP03 mission_metadata.py (#7445); WP04 cli/commands/glossary.py (#7463); WP05 Mission 058 roster data repair, planning_artifact owning only the six kitty-specs/058-hybrid-prompt-and-shim-agent-surface/tasks/WP0[1-6]-*.md files, depending on WP02. Each WP owns its tests and its issues' .fixed.md changelog fragments.

options: No: declare only real dependencies (WP05 on WP02) and let finalize-tasks settle topology by size
payload.question: Should dependencies be made artificially linear to keep the Mission single_branch?

payload.final_answer: No. Declare only the real dependency (WP05 depends on WP02). finalize-tasks settles the topology by size (ADR 2026-11-06-3); with four independent code WPs it is expected to settle lanes_with_coord. Artificial dependencies would misstate the work and serialise independent reviews.

options: New core module src/specify_cli/core/wp_task_files.py imported at module scope by subtask_rows, status/emit and status/wp_view
payload.question: Where does the shared WP task-file locator live?

payload.final_answer: A new core-layer module src/specify_cli/core/wp_task_files.py (stdlib + kernel._safe_re only) exposing one public matcher returning every name match, plus the separator pattern. core/subtask_rows.py, status/emit.py (_match_wp_files becomes a thin delegate or is replaced at its two call sites) and status/wp_view.py import it; the duplicate _WP_FILE_SEP in wp_view.py is removed. Keeps core free of status imports (C-007) and keeps emit's lazy subtask_rows import untouched.

options: normalize_authored_subtask_roster raises a SubtaskRosterResolutionError subclass; authored_subtask_roster adds the WP file name; _authored_group catches it and yields an empty tuple
payload.question: How do the gate and the WP view share one roster-entry rule while keeping their different failure contracts?

payload.final_answer: One rule in normalize_authored_subtask_roster: accept str and int (not bool), convert inside the guard so an over-limit int also refuses; raise a typed SubtaskRosterResolutionError subclass naming the entry position and the expected list form. authored_subtask_roster calls it inside its existing try and re-raises with the WP file name; status/wp_view._authored_group catches the typed error and yields an empty subtasks tuple. owning_wp_from_authored_roster already catches SubtaskRosterResolutionError and stays advisory.
